# mitos

> A framework for building Cardano indexers as **wasm modules paired
> with Cloudflare Worker companions**. The host (mitos) embeds Dolos
> as a chain follower, dispatches eUTXO events filtered by each
> module's declared interest, and POSTs the module's typed emissions
> to your CF Worker. Your Worker's Durable Objects consume those
> events, persist application state, and serve your read API.
>
> Two paths to a module:
>
> - **Community module** — generic chain recognition (e.g.
>   `asset-transfer`, `jpg-store-offer`, `holder-distribution`) lives
>   in `community-modules/<name>/` in this repo. Multiple dApps
>   subscribe to the same module via their own companion.
> - **dApp-owned module** — single-purpose recognition specific to
>   one dApp, lives in the dApp's own repo alongside its companion.
>
> In both cases the wasm module and the companion reference one
> shared event-types crate (`mitos-community-events` for the
> community path; a dApp-local crate for the bespoke path) so the
> wire shape can't drift.

## When to use mitos

Use mitos when you need to project on-chain data into a queryable
service:

- **A queryable view over chain state** — "who currently owns each
  asset under policy P," "all marketplace listings for collection C,"
  "all jpg.store collection offers on contract address A," etc.
- **A pipeline that runs on every block** with low latency and no
  re-derivation cost — your indexer code touches Dolos's lookup
  primitives directly (no gRPC / REST hops) and emits typed events
  to your consumer immediately.
- **A consumer service that lives at the edge** — your CF Worker
  Durable Objects hold the materialised view, serve your dApp's
  HTTP / WS surface, and stay warm via Hibernation.

Don't use mitos for ad-hoc one-shot queries — Dolos's HTTP APIs are
fine for that.

## How to build an indexer (the canonical path)

### 1. Pick the module side

If the recognition is generic (other dApps might want the same
event stream), write the module in this repo under
`community-modules/<name>/` and add its event submodule to
`crates/mitos-community-events/src/lib.rs`. See
`docs/strategy/COMMUNITY_MODULES.md`.

If the recognition is bespoke (one dApp, one purpose), keep it in
the dApp's own repo. Single-file: `<name>.rs` is the source of
truth. `mitos-build` materialises a Cargo crate around it at build
time, injects the WIT bindgen header, and ships the bundled host
WIT in-tree.

In both cases the module implements `Guest` from
`mitos:platform-v2/mitos-module-v2`. Hot path is
`handle-events(events: list<dispatch-event>)` — the platform
filters TXs against the module's declared interest, then dispatches
typed events (`produced`, `consumed`, `referenced`, `minted`,
`tx-context`, `tick`, `rollback`) in deterministic order. Dynamic
interest comes through `update-interest(op, items-cbor)` — pushed
in by the companion. Self-bootstrapping modules implement
`rebootstrap()` for recapture refills.

State is held in `state-kv` (per-module redb-backed) and snapshot
chain-state reads ride the `chain-data` host interface
(`utxos-by-address`, `utxos-by-policy`, `read-utxos`, `tx-metadata`,
`read-tx`, etc.). Canonical references:

- Community: `community-modules/asset-transfer/asset_transfer.rs`,
  `community-modules/jpg-store-offer/jpg_store_offer.rs`,
  `community-modules/holder-distribution/holder_distribution.rs`.
- Companions: `cnft.dev-workers/workers/collections-mitos/` (the
  collection-ownership worker subscribed to `asset-transfer`) and
  `cnft.dev-workers/workers/jpg-store-mirror/` (subscribed to
  `jpg-store-offer`).

### 2. Write the CF Worker companion

Worker embeds a `MitosCompanionRuntime<C>` inside a non-generic
`#[durable_object]` wrapper. The runtime owns:

- HTTP delivery surface (`POST /_internal/apply-<channel>` +
  `POST /_internal/recapture-<channel>`)
- HTTPS subscribe call to the host
- Cursor coordination
- Schema migration
- Auth (CF Secrets Store)
- Dynamic interest mutation

You implement `MitosCompanion` (`NAME`, `Config`, `channels()`,
`client_id()`, optionally `subscribe_targets()` / `on_recapture()`)
and `MitosChannel` per channel — each channel typed over its
`Event` shape. The channel's `apply_event` does the SQL writes;
the runtime handles cursor advance + Ack atomicity by HTTP status
(200 = Ack, 422 = Nack, 5xx = transport retry).

`client_id` is required: distinct `client_id` values let two
consumers share the same `companion_key` without collision (e.g.
dev + prod instances). See `docs/design/MULTI_CLIENT_COMPANIONS.md`.

### 3. Deploy

```bash
# Build + upload the wasm module
nix develop -c cargo run -p mitos-admin -- \
    --mitos https://mitos.defrag.cc --token "$TOKEN" \
    deploy --crate-name <crate-name>

# Deploy the worker
cd workers/my-dapp && wrangler deploy
```

The worker's first DO wake POSTs `SubscribeRequest` (CBOR, includes
`client_id`) to the host's `/api/companions/subscribe`. The host
persists the registration and starts POSTing emissions to the
worker's `/_internal/apply-<target>` endpoint per the dial-back URL
template (`MITOS_REPLICATE_URL`, e.g.
`https://hooks.example.com/_internal/{op}-{target}?key={key}`).

## Docs to read in order

### To understand the model
- [Companion pattern](docs/strategy/MITOS_COMPANION_PATTERN.md) — why dApps pair a wasm module with a CF Worker companion. **Start here** for any new project.
- [Cardano dApp framework thesis](docs/strategy/CARDANO_DAPP_FRAMEWORK_THESIS.md) — why this shape exists.
- [Layered responsibilities](docs/strategy/LAYERED_RESPONSIBILITIES.md) — what lives in mitos vs. community modules vs. dApp companions.

### To build the wasm module side
- [Platform v2](docs/strategy/MITOS_PLATFORM_V2.md) — current wasm-module runtime, eUTXO event-stream dispatch, WIT ABI, resource limits, trap policies.
- [Module deployment](docs/strategy/MITOS_PLATFORM_DEPLOYMENT.md) — `mitos-build` + `mitos-admin upload-module` flow.
- [Community modules](docs/strategy/COMMUNITY_MODULES.md) — when to put recognition in this repo vs. the dApp's repo.
- [WIT contract](crates/mitos-platform/wit-v2/world.wit) — exact ABI (v2): six exports (`module-version`, `trap-policy`, `init`, `handle-events`, `update-interest`, `rebootstrap`), host fns (`chain-data`, `state-kv`, `emit`, `logging`).
- [WASM budget chunking](docs/design/WASM_BUDGET_CHUNKING.md) — re-entrant `rebootstrap` + chunked snapshot emission for large policies.

### To build the CF Worker companion side
- [Companion runtime](docs/strategy/MITOS_COMPANION_RUNTIME_V1.md) — `MitosCompanionRuntime`, channels, subscribe call, dynamic interest, Ack/Nack via HTTP status.
- [HOWTO: consuming a community module](docs/HOWTO_CONSUMING_A_COMMUNITY_MODULE.md) — concrete step-by-step for the most common case (subscribe to a community module from a CF Worker).
- [Multi-client companions](docs/design/MULTI_CLIENT_COMPANIONS.md) — `client_id` keying so multiple consumers can share a `companion_key`.

### To operate a deployment
- `scripts/deploy.sh` — canonical deploy script; full operator procedure in `~/code/defrag/infra/docs/mitos-operations.md`.
- [Recapture procedure](docs/design/RECAPTURE.md) — operator-driven coordinated state rebuild via `mitos-admin recapture <id>`.
- [redb access pattern](docs/design/REDB_ACCESS.md) — host's storage discipline; relevant if you touch host code.

## Reference dApps

Most companions consume a **community module** from this repo. The
two canonical examples:

- `cnft.dev-workers/workers/collections-mitos/` — subscribes to
  `asset-transfer`; projects collection-ownership state. The
  `MitosCompanion` + `MitosChannel` impls live in `src/do_state.rs`;
  the wrangler config exposes `MITOS_HOST_URL` + `MITOS_REPLICATE_URL`
  + the `MITOS_AUTH_TOKEN` secrets store binding.
- `cnft.dev-workers/workers/jpg-store-mirror/` — subscribes to
  `jpg-store-offer`; mirrors active collection offers.

A dApp-owned module (single-purpose, in the dApp's repo) follows
the same companion shape; the only difference is that the
`.rs` source for the module sits next to the worker code rather
than under `community-modules/` in this repo.

## Static indexers — retired

The three legacy static indexers (`collection-ownership-indexer`,
`marketplace-indexer`, `mint-burn-indexer`) and the outbound
`mitos-core::Replicator` subscription model retired once their
consumers cut over to platform-v2 community modules (the
collection-ownership worker now subscribes to `asset-transfer`;
the jpg-store-mirror worker subscribes to `jpg-store-offer`;
mint/burn surfaces are covered by `cip-25-mint`, `cip-68-mint`,
`standard-burn`, `burn-address`, and `asset-metadata-update`).

The `none-match-indexer` stays as the dispatcher's residual-pass
coordinator — it emits `Domain::AssetMovement` for asset transfers
that no specific-domain indexer claims, and the v2 synchronised
dispatcher requires it (see `docs/design/DOMAIN_REFACTOR.md`).

Don't build new indexers as static crates. The wasm-module path is
the steady state — single-file source, hot-load via `mitos-admin
upload-module`, paired with a CF Worker companion in the dApp's
own repo.

## Active host

- Host: `https://mitos.defrag.cc` (Cloudflare-tunnelled to a netcup
  box running the bundle binary)
- Auth: shared bearer token via `MITOS_AUTH_TOKEN`
- Operator surface: `mitos-admin {health, list-modules, get-module,
  upload-module, restart-module, recapture, delete-module,
  evict-module, delete-companion, deploy, emissions,
  emissions-replay, emissions-purge}` — see
  `tools/mitos-admin/src/main.rs` for full subcommand details.
